{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "FULL WEBSITE BRIEF – Corporate Yoga Studio Event Showcase (Static Front-End Only)

Create a polished, corporate-style static website for a premium yoga studio hosting a flagship wellness event called “BalanceWorks Corporate Yoga Summit 2026”. The website should feel professional, calm, trustworthy, and elegant — suitable for HR teams, executives, office managers, and corporate wellness buyers who want to explore the event and register interest. This is NOT a backend app. Build only a static front-end website using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. All content, speakers, packages, schedules, testimonials, and form behavior can be mock/static/sample data. The form does not need to submit anywhere; show a nice success message on submit.

OVERALL GOAL
Design a product-showcase style event landing website for a yoga studio’s corporate wellness summit. The event is a one-day curated experience combining yoga, breathwork, mindfulness workshops, ergonomic movement, stress reduction talks, and team-building wellness sessions. The site should sell the event as a premium corporate offering, with clear sections explaining what is included, who it is for, why companies should attend, and how to request a seat/package.

BRAND STYLE
Brand name: BalanceWorks Studio
Event name: Corporate Yoga Summit 2026
Tone: corporate, calm, high-end, credible, wellness-focused
Visual style: modern corporate wellness, not hippie, not overly spiritual, not childish
Palette: soft ivory background, deep forest green, muted sage, warm beige, charcoal text, small gold accents
Typography: elegant but readable, large confident headings, clean body text
Layout: premium landing page with strong hierarchy, generous spacing, cards, subtle shadows, calm gradients
Mood: professional wellness retreat meets business conference
Use smooth section transitions, tasteful hover states, soft rounded corners, subtle animated reveals if possible with vanilla JS/CSS only

TECH REQUIREMENTS
Use vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript only.
No React, no Vue, no Angular.
No backend, no login, no database, no external APIs.
No real payment, no booking engine, no authentication.
No maps API; if location is shown, use a static styled location card.
No external services required to render.
Images can be placeholders, CSS gradients, simple SVG shapes, or local/static references. Use mock content.
Must be responsive: desktop, tablet, mobile.
Must be a complete static site, ideally organized as index.html, styles.css, script.js.

PAGE STRUCTURE / SECTIONS

1. Top Navigation
Sticky or elegant top navigation with logo text “BalanceWorks Studio”.
Nav items: Overview, Agenda, Sessions, Packages, Speakers, Venue, Register.
CTA button in nav: “Request Invitation”.
Mobile hamburger menu should work with vanilla JS.
Corporate feel, translucent/blurred header on scroll would be nice.

2. Hero Section
Large premium hero area.
Headline: “Corporate Yoga Summit 2026”
Subheadline: “A one-day wellness event designed for calmer teams, sharper focus, and healthier workplace culture.”
Include event date: Thursday, 22 October 2026
Include location: The Atrium Conference Hall, London
Include two CTA buttons: “View Event Packages” and “Register Interest”
Add small trust badges like: “For HR Leaders”, “Executive Teams”, “Workplace Wellness Programs”.
Hero visual should feel like a corporate wellness event: layered cards, abstract yoga silhouette, soft gradient, schedule preview, attendee stat cards etc. No need for real images.

3. Corporate Value Proposition
Section title: “Wellness That Works Inside the Workplace”
Explain in 3 or 4 cards why corporate yoga matters:
- Reduce stress and burnout
- Improve posture and mobility
- Support focus and emotional balance
- Build a healthier team culture
Each card should have an icon-style element, title, paragraph, and subtle hover interaction.

4. Event Overview / Product Showcase
Make the event feel like a premium product package.
Include a large feature block with:
- Full-day guided summit
- Yoga and mobility sessions for all levels
- Mindfulness and breathwork workshops
- Corporate wellness strategy panel
- Healthy networking lounge
- Take-home digital wellness toolkit (static mention only)
Use a comparison-style layout or feature grid.
Add a small “Designed for companies of 10–500+ employees” label.

5. Agenda Timeline
Create an elegant timeline for the day. Use static sample agenda:
08:30 – Arrival Tea & Grounding
09:15 – Opening Keynote: The Future of Workplace Wellbeing
10:00 – Desk Body Reset Yoga
11:15 – Breathwork for High-Pressure Teams
12:30 – Nourish Lunch & Networking
13:45 – Mindful Leadership Lab
15:00 – Corporate Mobility Workshop
16:15 – Team Calm Challenge
17:00 – Closing Reflection & Next Steps
The timeline should look premium and responsive.

6. Featured Sessions
Create product cards for individual sessions. At least 6 cards:
- Executive Reset Flow
- Desk-to-Mat Mobility
- Breathwork Under Pressure
- Mindful Leadership Lab
- Team Recovery Stretch
- Workplace Wellness Strategy Panel
Each card includes duration, level, best for, short description, and a small “included” tag.
Add filter chips visually such as “All”, “Movement”, “Mindfulness”, “Leadership”, “Team Building”. Filters can work with simple vanilla JS or just visual, but working static filter would be nice.

7. Packages / Pricing Showcase
Include 3 corporate event packages. Make clear these are sample/static packages and “request pricing” style, not real checkout.
Packages:
Essential Team Pass
- Up to 10 attendees
- Access to all core sessions
- Digital wellness guide
- Healthy refreshment access
Growth Company Pass
- Up to 35 attendees
- Reserved seating zone
- Team reflection workbook
- Priority workshop selection
Executive Wellness Partner
- Up to 75 attendees
- Private pre-event consultation
- Branded team welcome pack
- Post-event wellbeing summary template
Add CTA on each: “Request Package Info”. Buttons should scroll to the form and prefill/select package if possible with JS.
No payment integration.

8. Speakers / Facilitators
Corporate-looking speaker cards with mock people, roles, and bios. Use realistic but fictional names:
- Maya Ellison, Lead Corporate Yoga Facilitator
- Dr. Arun Patel, Workplace Stress Researcher
- Lena Hoffmann, Breathwork Coach
- Marcus Reed, Mindful Leadership Consultant
- Sofia Green, Mobility & Ergonomics Specialist
Cards should include topic, years experience, and simple avatar placeholder.

9. Venue Experience
Section about venue and atmosphere.
Use static content only:
The Atrium Conference Hall, London
Describe calm arrival lounge, natural light, quiet rooms, hydration stations, mat-ready studio area, networking corners.
Add a static “location card” with address text, travel notes, and parking note. No live map.

10. Testimonials / Trust Section
Add 4 testimonials from fictional corporate clients, e.g. HR Director, People Ops Lead, Finance Team Manager.
Mention outcomes like improved team connection, calmer planning week, better posture awareness.
Also include trust metrics as static numbers:
120+ corporate teams hosted
4.9/5 average attendee rating
8 guided wellness formats
92% would recommend to colleagues

11. Who Should Attend
Create segmented audience cards:
- HR & People Teams
- Executive Leadership Groups
- Office Managers
- Remote/Hybrid Team Leads
- Employee Resource Groups
- Corporate Wellness Consultants
Each should explain why the summit fits them.

12. Registration / Interest Form
Important interaction: form must be included and feel polished.
Fields:
Full Name
Work Email
Company Name
Role / Department
Estimated Attendees dropdown: 1–10, 11–35, 36–75, 75+
Interested Package dropdown: Essential Team Pass, Growth Company Pass, Executive Wellness Partner, Not Sure Yet
Preferred Contact Method: Email / Phone / Either
Message textarea
Checkbox: “I agree to be contacted about this event.”
Submit button: “Request Invitation”
Use client-side validation with vanilla JS: required fields, email format, checkbox required.
On success, show a clean confirmation panel/message like: “Thank you — your interest request has been prepared. A BalanceWorks coordinator would contact you in a real deployment.” Do not actually send anywhere.
If package buttons are clicked earlier, scroll to this form and update the package dropdown.

13. FAQ Section
Accordion interaction with vanilla JS.
Questions:
Is this event suitable for beginners?
Can we bring a mixed-experience team?
Are mats provided?
Can companies sponsor a private table?
Is food included?
Can the summit be adapted for remote teams?
Make answers corporate and concise.

14. Footer
Include logo/name, short description, event date/location, quick links, contact placeholder email hello@balanceworks.example, and social placeholders. No real external links needed.
Add note: “Static demo website — sample event content.”

INTERACTION DETAILS
- Smooth scrolling for nav links and CTA buttons.
- Mobile menu open/close.
- FAQ accordion.
- Package CTA scrolls to form and selects package.
- Session filters if feasible using data attributes.
- Form validation and success state.
- Header style changes slightly on scroll.
- No backend submission.

DESIGN QUALITY EXPECTATIONS
Make it look like a finished corporate marketing site, not a basic template. Use professional spacing, consistent card design, strong hero composition, visually rich but calm sections, accessible contrast, responsive layout, and polished form styling. Include microcopy that sounds believable for a real yoga studio selling a corporate event.

DELIVERABLE
A complete static website that can be opened locally in the browser. Please create clean files and code comments only where useful. Must not rely on live APIs, accounts, databases, or server-side functionality.",
 "judge": {
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8",
  "model_sha": "94125d2bd83076b21eed33119525e29eaf3894f4",
  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
